summary: The note describes the growing push to integrate cybersecurity into school curricula, beginning in the 2023-2024 academic year, driven by rising online threats to young users. It covers key educators, game-based tools like CyberHero, funding through the SafeNet Initiative, teacher training, early successes, and a vision of cyber-resilient students and eventual national and international curricula.
one_line: Schools are embedding cybersecurity into core curricula from 2023-2024, using interactive tools, teacher training and grants to build cyber-resilient students.
key_facts: Starting in the 2023-2024 academic year, numerous educational institutions began rolling out programs that integrate cybersecurity into subjects such as computer science, social studies, and literature.
Dr. Sarah Jennings, a cybersecurity expert and curriculum advisor, is a leading educator spearheading the initiative.
On September 5, 2023, the National Cyber Security Alliance reported an alarming uptick in incidents involving younger internet users, prompting a call-to-action for schools.

Dr. Jennings said at a conference on September 12 that cybersecurity education is about "empowering our children with the knowledge and skills they need to navigate and shape the digital world responsibly."
Marcus Thompson leads the initiative at Riverside Middle School and works with IT professionals to create grade-appropriate cybersecurity lesson plans.
The CyberHero initiative, launched on November 1, 2023, uses a gamification platform where students go on digital quests that teach cybersecurity.
Rachel Simmons, a technology educator at West Valley High School, says hands-on, interactive methods drive engagement better than lectures.
David Chen, who advises school districts on technological integration, said in December that the cost of integrating cybersecurity is minimal compared to the consequences of cyber ignorance.
The SafeNet Initiative, introduced by the federal government in early 2024, gives schools financial aid and resources to develop cybersecurity curricula.
Alan Rodriguez, a computer science teacher, spent the first quarter of the year attending workshops to understand cybersecurity before teaching it.
Under the CyberKids program, Mary and her classmates at Sunnydale Elementary identified phishing emails that had reached school administrative staff.
Students from several pilot schools have joined nationwide cybersecurity competitions, some collaborating with local businesses to improve their online security.
